notes:
CIRCUIT: a multi-stage bias/logic ladder. A resistive chain hangs off the +15 V top rail: 15k (#1) down to the +10 V node, 15k (#4) down to node n5, 150 Ohm (#9) across to the +6 V node, 15k (#8) across to the +5 V node. Four PNPs (#11 #12 #13 #15) and five NPNs (#3 #17 #18 #19 #21) plus two series diodes (#5 #10) hang between those bias nodes and a common bottom rail. There is NO GND symbol on this sheet, so no net is named '0'; the bottom rail is just another net (n15). 22 components, 16 nets.

NET MAP:
  n1  = the +15 V top rail (y~222, x 277..830) plus the arrow lead of #0: 0.0, 15k #1 top (1.0), #3 collector (3.0).
  n2  = the +10 V node (the column between the two 15k resistors, x~270, y 294..366, plus the +10 V arrow lead): 1.1, 2.0, 4.0.
  n3  = #3 base wire: from #3's base bar left along y~386 to x~713, then down to the anode of diode #5: 3.1, 5.0.
  n4  = the +5 V node: the vertical at x~827 from #3's emitter (829,436) down to #13's emitter and #17's collector at (819,598), plus the +5 V arrow lead of #7 arriving from the right, plus the right end of 15k #8: 3.2, 7.0, 8.1, 13.2, 17.0.
  n5  = the tap between 15k #4 and 150 Ohm #9: the column x~277 y 429..524 -> #11's emitter: 4.1, 9.0, 11.2.
  n6  = between the two series diodes (x~712, y 450..530): 5.1, 10.1.
  n7  = the +6 V node (x~481, y 484) where the +6 V arrow, 150 Ohm right end, 15k #8 left end and #12's emitter column meet: 6.0, 8.0, 9.1, 12.2.
  n8  = cathode of diode #10 -> down to #18's collector, with a branch right at y~652 to #13's base: 10.0, 13.1, 18.0.
  n9  = #11's collector down to #21's collector (x~280, y 630..756): 11.0, 21.0.
  n10 = #11's base wire: left from (239,578) to x~195, then down to #15's emitter at (197,625): 11.1, 15.2.
  n11 = #12's collector down to (481,713), right to (513,713), down to (513,795), then right along y~784 (passing UNDER the 50k column) to #18's base; #19's collector joins the same node from below at (485,715): 12.0, 18.1, 19.0.
  n12 = #12's base wire right from (517,586) then down to the top of the 50k #16: 12.1, 16.0.
  n13 = #13's collector down to #17's base (x~782, y 697..789): 13.0, 17.1.
  n14 = the +3 V node (114,678): the +3 V arrow lead, #15's base wire to the right, and the top of 50k #20: 14.0, 15.1, 20.0.
  n15 = the common bottom rail (y~865, x 113..820): #15 collector (15.0), 50k #16 bottom (16.1), and the emitters of #17, #18, #19, #21 (17.2, 18.2, 19.2, 21.2), plus 50k #20 bottom (20.1).
  n16 = the wire tying #21's base (324,792) to #19's base (457,788): 19.1, 21.1.

CRITICAL SITES (explicit decisions):
  S1  (586,231) -> JUNCTION. Fat solder blob (dot=1.8) where the +15 V arrow lead lands on the top rail. T shape, nothing continues above. Crossing would strand #0 on a one-terminal net.
  S4  (269,340) -> JUNCTION. Clear round solder dot (dot=2.2) at the +10 V tap between 15k #1 and 15k #4. Crossing would strand the +10 V source.
  S8  (279,471) -> JUNCTION. Dot present; the 150 Ohm branch leaves the #4/#11 column here. Crossing would strand the 150 Ohm left end.
  S10 (481,484) -> JUNCTION. Big solder dot; four branches (+6 V arrow, 150 Ohm right, 15k #8 left, #12 emitter column). hop_score 5.7 is just the kink where the +6 V lead is drawn; there is no arc. Crossing would split the +6 V node and leave #6 on a two-terminal stub.
  S11 (719,496) -> CROSSING. Verified in pixels (inkmap at 719,494): the diode column runs down at x~711, steps sideways to x~720 at y 483-486, passes the horizontal 15k wire at y 495-499, then steps back left to x~709 at y 501-507. That sideways jog is the drafter's 'not connected' mark; the same drafter puts a fat blob on every real junction on this sheet (S1, S4, S10, S16, S18, S19, S20, S30..S34) and there is no blob here (dot=1.1). Junction would tie the diode string to the +6 V/+5 V resistor and short out both diodes.
  S16 (827,522) -> JUNCTION. Solder dot on the +5 V column where #7's lead arrives from the right. See also bridge B11 below.
  S18 (818,600) -> JUNCTION. Solder dot; #13's emitter lead comes in from the left and meets the +5 V column, which continues down to #17's collector.
  S19 (697,649) -> JUNCTION. Solder dot; the diode-#10 cathode column continues down to #18's collector and a branch runs right to #13's base.
  S20 (114,678) -> JUNCTION. Largest dot on the sheet (2.5); +3 V arrow, #15 base wire and the top of 50k #20 meet.
  S23 (483,712) -> JUNCTION. T: #12's collector comes down, #19's collector comes up, and the branch to #18's base leaves to the right. Crossing would cut #18's base off from the collectors.
  S26 (597,782) + S27 (588,786) -> CROSSING, expressed as explicit edge groups because the single drawn hop was split into two sites. Groups: [[65,71,73],[69,70]] on S26 and 'none' on S27. e65 = 50k column above the hop (586,725)->(598,780); e71 = the short return diagonal of the hop (595,784)->(590,786); e73 = 50k column below the hop (587,788)->(586,869); e69 = horizontal right half to #18's base (658,783)->(599,783); e70 = horizontal left half (518,788)->(586,784). Evidence: both crops show an unmistakable semicircular bulge, and inkmap at (594,784) shows the column stepping right from x=585 to x=597 above the horizontal and back left to x=586 below it. Electrical check: reading it as a junction merges n11 into the bottom rail, which shorts #19's collector to its own emitter and puts #18's base on the same net as #18's emitter - both transistors would be dead shorts. Crossing is the only sane reading and it is also what the ink says.
  S30 (283,861), S31 (486,864), S33 (585,871), S34 (697,876) -> JUNCTION. All four are dotted Ts where a column (#21 emitter, #19 emitter, 50k #16 bottom, #18 emitter) lands on the bottom rail.
  S32 (192,870) -> JUNCTION. #15's collector column crosses the bottom rail with a few px of pen overshoot below it (hop=2.1 is that overshoot, not an arc; no bulge in the crop, and the dot score is 2.2). Crossing would leave #15's collector alone with a 5px tail, i.e. a one-terminal net.
  Non-critical sites left at default: S0 (R1 top on the top rail, real T but the tracer joins it anyway), S3, S5, S6, S7, S9, S12, S13, S21, S22, S25, S28, S29 - every one of these is either handwritten label ink ('15 kOhm', '150 Ohm', '50 kOhm', '+10 V', '+6 V', '+5 V', '+3 V') brushing a wire, or an elbow inside a net that is already connected.

GAP BRIDGE:
  B11 (818,513)->(827,513), dist 9 -> KEPT. inkmap at (822,515) shows the right end of the 15k #8 wire stopping at x=818,y=514 with a 7-8 px paper gap before the +5 V column at x=826-828. The wire is unmistakably aimed at the column and there is nothing else within 50 px; dropping the bridge would leave 8.1 on a one-terminal net (a resistor with one end going nowhere), which the rest of the sheet contradicts - the bias chain 15V-15k-10V-15k-n5-150-6V-15k-5V only makes sense if the last resistor reaches the +5 V node. Kept as a junction.

PIN-ORDER FIXES (3-terminal parts; order IS scored):
  This drafter draws every BJT the same way: a vertical base bar with the base lead on one side and the two other leads leaving diagonally on the other side. On all four PNPs the solid arrowhead sits on the UPPER diagonal and points down-left INTO the base bar (verified at 20x on #15 at (183,646): the two barbs converge to a tip touching the bar), so the upper lead is the emitter. On all five NPNs the arrowhead sits on the LOWER diagonal and points AWAY from the bar (verified at 20x on #21 at (290,800)), so the lower lead is the emitter. Physical reading agrees everywhere: PNP emitters go to the higher-potential bias node, NPN emitters go to the bottom rail.
  #11 BJT-PNP: tracer had t0=top(emitter), t2=bottom(collector). Remapped to t0=p1 bottom = COLLECTOR, t1=p2 left = BASE, t2=p0 top = EMITTER.
  #12 BJT-PNP: remapped to t0=p0 bottom = COLLECTOR, t1=p2 right = BASE, t2=p1 top = EMITTER.
  #13 BJT-PNP: remapped to t0=p0 bottom = COLLECTOR, t1=p1 left = BASE, t2=p2 top = EMITTER.
  #15 BJT-PNP: remapped to t0=p0 bottom = COLLECTOR, t1=p1 left = BASE, t2=p2 top = EMITTER.
  #3, #17, #18, #19, #21 (BJT-NPN) were already collector/base/emitter and are left alone: #3 collector up to the +15 V rail, base left to the diode string, emitter down to +5 V; #17/#18/#19/#21 collectors up, bases sideways, emitters down to the bottom rail.

OTHER TRACER WARNINGS CHECKED: the 'unused port candidate' warnings on #1 (300,252), #4 (294,410)/(293,396) and #9 (340,502) are all strokes of the handwritten values '15 kOhm', '15 kOhm' and '150 Ohm'; the assigned ports are the real leads, so no change.

CLASSES: all 22 accepted. Arrow directions confirm the PNP/NPN split exactly as annotated; both triangle+bar symbols are plain Diodes (no zener tails); the five arrow-with-label symbols are one-port V-DC supplies (+15 V, +10 V, +6 V, +5 V, +3 V).

UNRESOLVED: nothing outstanding. The only judgement that is not pixel-certain is bridge B11 (a genuine 8 px paper gap that I read as pen underrun); it is documented above.
